propositions.text: RPD received an application to reopen the refugee claim of an Egyptian citizen on December 10, 2012.
propositions.quote: On December 10, 2012, the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) received an application to reopen the refugee protection claim of XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Egypt, in accordance with rule 55 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules (RPD Rules).

propositions.text: This application follows the RPD decision of November 30, 2012, declaring abandonment of her refugee claim.
propositions.quote: This application follows the RPD decision rendered on November 30, 2012, declaring the abandonment of her refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Notice of decision was sent to applicant on December 4, 2012.
propositions.quote: A notice of decision was sent to the applicant on December 4, 2012.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RPD received the reopening application on Dec 10, 2012, after an abandonment decision on Nov 30, 2012, with notice sent Dec 4, 2012.

propositions.text: RPD Rules were amended on December 15, 2012, so application analyzed under new rule 62.
propositions.quote: The RPD Rules were amended on December 15, 2012; as a result, this application will be analyzed in accordance with rule 62 of the new RPD Rules.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes RPD Rules amended Dec 15, 2012, so application analyzed under new rule 62.

propositions.text: RPD's jurisdiction to reopen claims is limited; subrule 62(6) requires failure to observe natural justice to allow reopening.
propositions.quote: The RPD's jurisdiction to reopen refugee protection claims is very limited. Subrule 62(6) of the RPD Rules states that the application to reopen must not be allowed unless it is established that there was a failure to observe a principle of natural justice.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RPD can only reopen claims if a natural justice failure is established under subrule 62(6).

propositions.text: Once RPD renders decision, it is functus officio and cannot reconsider unless natural justice violated.
propositions.quote: case law1 states that once the RPD has rendered a decision, it has discharged its duty (functus officio) and cannot exercise it a second time in the same case, unless there was a violation of the rules of natural justice.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites case law that RPD cannot reconsider a case after decision unless natural justice was violated.

propositions.text: Minister opposes reopening, alleging no failure to observe natural justice.
propositions.quote: The Minister responded to the application to reopen on December 18, 2012, and opposes this reopening, alleging that there was no failure to observe a principle of natural justice.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister opposes reopening, arguing no natural justice failure occurred.

propositions.text: Applicant's affidavit states she did not receive notices to appear for hearings on Nov 15 and Nov 30, 2012.
propositions.quote: To support her application to reopen, the applicant submitted an affidavit dated December 10, 2012, in which she states that she did not receive the notice to appear for her hearing on November 15, 2012. She also did not receive the notice to appear for the abandonment hearing set for November 30, 2012

propositions.text: Applicant received notice of decision at new address, submitted as P-4.
propositions.quote: but she states that she received, at her new address, the notice of decision concerning the abandonment of her refugee protection claim, submitted under P-4.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states in affidavit she did not receive hearing notices but did receive the decision notice at new address.

propositions.text: Applicant lived at daughter's home until XXXX 2012, then had argument and was forced to leave.
propositions.quote: The applicant explained that she had been living at her daughter's home until XXXX 2012. On XXXX XXXX, 2012, she allegedly had an argument with her daughter and son-in-law, and they allegedly forced her to leave the home.

propositions.text: Applicant filed police complaint about being forced to leave, but no police report submitted.
propositions.quote: She stated that she filed a complaint about this with the police. However, the panel notes that no police report on this matter accompanies the affidavit.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant says she was forced to leave daughter's home and filed police complaint, but no police report was submitted.

propositions.text: Applicant stayed one night in shelter, then with church people; priest helped find housing.
propositions.quote: The applicant stated that she stayed one night in a shelter and that the next day she allegedly went to stay at the home of people from her church. On XXXX XXXX, 2012, the priest at that church allegedly helped her find housing.

propositions.text: Priest's letter states he met applicant first on XXXX XXXX, 2012, took her to family home, then helped find apartment.
propositions.quote: The applicant submitted a letter from him under P-2. The panel notes that he states that he met Ms. XXXX (the applicant) for the first time on XXXX XXXX, 2012, that she spoke to him about the problems that she allegedly had with her daughter and son-in-law, and that she had no place to go. At that point, he allegedly took her to the home of a family, and she stayed there until he found her an apartment, on XXXX XXXX, 2012.

propositions.text: Lease signed on XXXX XXXX, 2012, submitted as P-3.
propositions.quote: A lease was signed on XXXX XXXX, 2012, and submitted with this application under P-3.

propositions.text: Panel notes minor discrepancy between applicant's affidavit and priest's letter about dates of stay with church people.
propositions.quote: The panel notes a minor discrepancy between the facts related by the applicant in her affidavit and what the priest stated in his letter-according to the applicant, she went to stay with people from the church on XXXX XXXX, 2012.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant says she stayed with church people; priest confirms and helped find housing; panel notes minor date discrepancy.

propositions.text: Applicant notified social assistance of address change to continue cheques.
propositions.quote: The applicant stated that she notified social assistance of her change of address in order to continue to receive her social assistance cheques.

propositions.text: Applicant's daughter helped with refugee claim; applicant did not know how to communicate with lawyer or CIC.
propositions.quote: She stated that her daughter had been helping her with her refugee protection claim and, therefore, she did not know how to communicate with her lawyer or with Citizenship and Immigration Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant notified social assistance of address change but did not know how to communicate with lawyer or CIC due to daughter's help.

propositions.text: Panel puzzled by applicant's claim because Minister says applicant notified Minister of address change on XXXX XXXX, 2012, with notice submitted as M-1.
propositions.quote: The panel is puzzled by this allegation because the Minister indicates in the Minister's response that the applicant notified the Minister of her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012-a copy of the notice was submitted under M-1.

propositions.text: Applicant's notice shows new and previous addresses; RPD had different former address on file.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that the applicant indicates on that notice that her new address is XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and that her previous address was XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, while the RPD had XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, as her former address.

propositions.text: Minister notes applicant had not provided CIC with change of address; M-2 printout shows address history with no record of stay at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the Minister noted this and indicates in paragraph 10 of the Minister's response that the applicant had not yet provided CIC with her change of address; to this effect, the Minister submitted M-2, a printout from the Field Operations Support System (FOSS) that shows that, on XXXX XXXX, 2011, the applicant was living at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX, and that, on XXXX XXXX, 2012, her new address was XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX. There is no record of her stay at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Panel notes Minister's evidence that applicant notified Minister but not CIC of address change; no record of stay at one address.

propositions.text: Minister points out no explanation for applicant's or counsel's communication attempts after move.
propositions.quote: The Minister also points out that there is no explanation for the steps that the applicant allegedly took to try to communicate with her counsel after she moved or for the steps that her counsel allegedly took to try to communicate with the applicant.

paragraphs.summary: Minister argues no explanation for communication attempts between applicant and counsel after move.

propositions.text: Applicant moved on XXXX XXXX, 2012, notified social assistance and CIC of address change despite affidavit claim.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that the claimant allegedly moved to XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, on XXXX XXXX, 2012. She provided social assistance with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012 (see P-3 submitted with this application). She provided CIC with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012, (M-1) despite the allegation in her affidavit that she did not know how to communicate with CIC.

propositions.text: After receiving notice of decision on Dec 4, 2012, applicant quickly communicated with lawyer to file reopening application by Dec 10, 2012, but counsel info not on notice.
propositions.quote: In addition, the panel notes that, after receiving the notice of decision sent on December 4, 2012, to her correct address, the applicant did not explain how, at that point, she was able to communicate with her lawyer very quickly, because an application to reopen was received by the RPD on December 10, 2012. Neither the name nor the contact information of her counsel appears on that notice of decision (see P-1 submitted with this application).

paragraphs.summary: Panel finds applicant notified social assistance and CIC of address change and quickly filed reopening after decision notice, but counsel info missing.

propositions.text: Subrule 4(3) requires claimants to provide new contact info in writing to RPD and Minister immediately upon change.
propositions.quote: Subrule 4(3) of the RPD Rules states that a claimant must provide their new contact information in writing to the RPD and to the Minister as soon as it changes.

propositions.text: Form IMM-5292 given to applicant states obligation to provide mailing address changes in writing to RPD and Minister.
propositions.quote: This rule is also clearly indicated on form IMM-5292,2 which was given to the applicant when she submitted her refugee protection claim, that is, that the applicant must provide her mailing address in writing to the RPD and to the Minister and that, as soon as her contact information changes, she must provide it in writing to the RPD and to the Minister.

propositions.text: Applicant provided Minister with address change before notice to appear mailed but failed to provide RPD with change in writing.
propositions.quote: In addition, according to the evidence submitted by the Minister, the applicant provided the Minister with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012, that is, before the notice to appear for the applicant's first hearing had been mailed. The applicant also should have provided her new contact information to the RPD.

propositions.text: Applicant had months between move and first hearing to notify RPD despite shock of move.
propositions.quote: The panel notes that XXXX months passed between when she moved on XXXX XXXX, 2012, and her first hearing set for November 15, 2012. She allegedly had sufficient time, despite the shock of the move, to take the necessary steps to communicate with the RPD, either on her own or with the help of the church priest.

paragraphs.summary: Court states rule requires claimant to notify RPD and Minister in writing of address changes; applicant notified Minister but not RPD despite time.

propositions.text: Evidence does not show failure to observe natural justice; notices sent to address on file.
propositions.quote: After reviewing the application to reopen, the Minister's response and the applicant's entire file, the panel is of the opinion that the evidence submitted does not demonstrate that there was a failure to observe the principles of natural justice. The notices to appear were sent to the applicant, to the address that the Board had on file.

propositions.text: Applicant provided Minister with address change but failed to notify RPD in writing; this is applicant's responsibility, not natural justice failure.
propositions.quote: The applicant provided the Minister with her change of address on XXXX XXXX, 2012, but failed to provide her change of address in writing to the RPD, as required under rule 4; this does not constitute a failure to observe a principle of natural justice but rather a fact that may be attributed to her and for which she alone is responsible.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes no natural justice failure; applicant responsible for not notifying RPD in writing of address change.

propositions.text: Application to reopen is dismissed.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the application to reopen is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application to reopen.
